name: Histiocytic Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of malignant histiocytic cells with characteristic morphology
Immunohistochemical positivity for histiocytic markers CD68, CD163, and lysozyme with absence of B-cell and T-cell markers
Exclusion of other hematologic malignancies such as lymphoma or dendritic cell sarcoma
Detection of clonal rearrangements or mutations supporting histiocytic lineage

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Morphologic evidence of malignant histiocytic cells with confirmatory immunophenotyping and exclusion of other hematologic malignancies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, immunophenotyping, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized or disseminated malignant histiocytic tumor masses
pathognomonic.notes: Masses may occur in lymph nodes, skin, or soft tissues
searchTerms: single or multiple malignant immune cell tumors

pathognomonic.symptomName: Immunohistochemical expression of CD163 and CD68 in tumor cells
searchTerms: tumor cells showing CD163 and CD68 markers
immune marker presence in tumor cells

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including fever and weight loss
searchTerms: fever, weight loss, and night sweats
general symptoms like tiredness and fever
systemic illness signs including weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to osseous involvement

searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to lung involvement

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits from central nervous system involvement
searchTerms: neurological problems from brain or spinal cord involvement
nerve function loss due to CNS disease
low red blood cells and other blood cells
blood loss from gut lining damage
vision issues due to eye disease

laboratory: Immunohistochemical positivity for CD68, CD163, and lysozyme
imaging: CT or MRI showing soft tissue masses or organ infiltration
genetic: Absence of B-cell and T-cell receptor gene rearrangements
other: Histopathological confirmation with malignant histiocytic morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of histiocytic markers CD163 and CD68
Expression of follicular dendritic cell markers (CD21, CD35)

redFlags: Failure to respond to standard lymphoma therapies
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
